content: 1. Do not store this medication in the bathroom or freeze it. Follow the specific storage instructions provided on the product packaging or consult your pharmacist for guidance. 2. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. 3. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. 4. This information was last updated in August 2024. 5. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. 7. Before taking erythromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any other substances. 8. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 9. Erythromycin may cause a condition affecting heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. 10. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood may also increase the risk of QT prolongation, especially if caused by diuretics, severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. 11. Erythromycin may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). 12. Some erythromycin products may contain sodium, which should be considered if you are on a sodium-restricted diet. 13. Infants may be at higher risk for a serious stomach condition when using this medication. 14. This medication passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. 15. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 16. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 17. Other medications may affect the removal of erythromycin from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. 18. Erythromycin may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, which could affect how they work. 19. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (e.g., urine tests), potentially causing false results. 20. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. 21. U.S. residents can call the Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222. 22. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it for other conditions unless directed by your doctor. 23. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 24.
